title: Pawn breakthrough

D0.outcome: Explains the breakthrough: sacrificing a pawn or two to create a passed pawn when several pawns face each other.

D1.outcome: Finds the breakthrough move in a 3-against-3 pawn skeleton when it exists.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled pawn endings, tells when a breakthrough wins, draws or loses, depending on who is nearer to queening and who has the move.

D3.outcome: Verifies the breakthrough by counting and predicts how one extra tempo for the defender changes the result.

misconceptions: The breakthrough always works if there are more pawns.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S7 (Chesscademy 'Opposition and Breakthrough', title only)
conditions: The attacker's pawns are further advanced; with the other side to move the same position is drawn.
contrasts: The same skeleton with the wrong side to move.

soft_prereq_notes.END.KPK.D1: the resulting passed pawn is a K+P problem
